item.title: Patchier permafrost is linked to more intense hillslope erosion in Alaska
item.description: The Arctic is warming four times faster than the rest of the globe, and scientists are racing to understand how that fact affects the region's landscapes and ecosystems. Permafrost thaw is one of the most visible signs of climate change, with whole hillslopes of previously frozen ground slumping off and coastlines falling into the ocean. It's disrupting ecosystems, releasing carbon, and threatening Indigenous communities in the far north. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Bacteria turn 3D-printed sand into solid building elements
item.description: Cement manufacturing is one of the largest sources of CO₂ emissions in the construction industry. item.title: Gathering rare airborne observations of firestorm clouds
item.description: Just minutes into a planned research flight from Colorado to Oregon in August to study massive storm clouds fueled by intense wildfires, scientists discovered that a fire in Utah offered a more promising target. The mission support staff on the ground scrambled to draw up a new flight plan, and the pilots of the U.S. National Science Foundation National Center for Atmospheric Research (NSF NCAR) Gulfstream V worked to get the green light from air traffic controllers to fly toward the wildfire-generated thunderstorm. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: The ocean circulation that persists even after a key AMOC component fails
item.description: The Atlantic meridional overturning circulation (AMOC) is thought to face a potentially existential threat from climate change. item.title: Major cities worldwide are sinking, satellite data reveal
item.description: Land subsidence is the gradual sinking of the ground, which can damage buildings, foundations, and drainage and sewage systems, and may increase flood risks. However, information on land subsidence dynamics remains limited, which makes it difficult for policymakers to identify where risks are intensifying and where urgent intervention may be needed. Previous assessments have often used different methods or time periods, or focused only on small numbers of cities, which has made global comparisons difficult. Fuente: Phys.org.
